definitions.explanation: A military branch or soldier specialized in operating large-caliber weapons such as cannons and howitzers. Can refer to either the branch of the military or an individual soldier.

examples.japanese: {砲兵|ほうへい}⟦{部隊|ぶたい}→部隊：28119_butai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{配置|はいち}→配置：14409_haichi⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
{砲兵|ほうへい}⟦による→による：28349_niyoru⟧⟦{支援|しえん}→支援：07778_shien⟧⟦{射撃|しゃげき}→射撃：16089_shageki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{行|おこな}われた→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: Supporting fire was carried out by the artillery.

examples.japanese: ⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、ナポレオン⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{砲兵|ほうへい}{士官|しかん}だったこと⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}んだ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
examples.english: In history class, I learned that Napoleon was an artillery officer.

notes:
FORMS:
{砲|ほう} (cannon, artillery piece) + ⟦{兵|へい}→兵：29510_hei⟧ (soldier, troops).

USAGE:
Appears in historical texts, military discussions, and news about armed conflicts. In modern Japanese ⟦{自衛隊|じえいたい}→自衛隊：05790_jieitai⟧, the equivalent is {特科|とっか} (special branch/artillery).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{歩兵|ほへい}→歩兵：13223_hohei⟧: infantry
- ⟦{騎兵|きへい}→騎兵：18012_kihei⟧: cavalry
- {工兵|こうへい}: combat engineers

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {砲兵|ほうへい}⟦{部隊|ぶたい}→部隊：28119_butai⟧: artillery unit
- {砲兵|ほうへい}⟦{陣地|じんち}→陣地：30721_jinchi⟧: artillery position
- {砲兵|ほうへい}{士官|しかん}: artillery officer
